title: Rust Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Print a greeting
entries.summary: println! prints text and starts a new line. main is the program entry point.
notes: println! has an exclamation mark because it is a macro.

entries.name: Keep a value
entries.summary: let creates a name for a value. Values cannot be changed unless you ask for mut.
notes: A plain let binding cannot be assigned a new value.

entries.name: Change a value
entries.summary: mut means this binding may change. It makes the choice to change data clear.
notes: Use mut only when the value needs to change.

entries.name: Pick a value with if
entries.summary: if can produce a value. Both branches here return text of the same type.
notes: Both branches used as a value must have matching types.

entries.name: Count with a range
entries.summary: 1..=3 includes both ends. A for loop visits each number in the range.

entries.name: Grow a list
entries.summary: A Vec stores values in order. push adds a value at the end.
notes: The vector must be mutable to push a new item.

entries.name: Return a result
entries.summary: The last expression can be a function result. It has no trailing semicolon.

example.code:
fn twice(n: i32) -> i32 { n * 2 }
fn main() { println!("{}", twice(4)); }

notes: A semicolon after n * 2 turns it into a statement with no returned number.

entries.name: Move ownership
entries.summary: A String owns its text. Assigning it to another variable moves that ownership.
notes: Do not use a String binding after its value has moved.

entries.name: Read without taking ownership
entries.summary: A reference borrows a value. It lets code read the value while its owner keeps it.
notes: A reference must not outlive the value it points to.

entries.name: Handle a missing value
entries.summary: Option holds Some(value) or None. unwrap_or gives a fallback for None.
notes: unwrap can panic on None; check it or use a fallback.

entries.name: Handle a failed action
entries.summary: Result holds Ok for success or Err for failure. Parsing text can fail.
notes: Do not assume every text value is a valid number.

entries.name: Group named data
entries.summary: A struct describes named fields. Each Book value can hold its own title.
notes: Supply every required field when making a struct.
